newsitem.title: USA: U.S. 1996 crop, wheat seedings, stocks - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. 1996 crop, wheat seedings, stocks - USDA.

text.p: USDA on Friday pegged 1996 U.S. corn production at 9.293 billion bushels and soybeans at 2.382 billion in its final estimates of last year's crops.
The corn estimate was slightly below trade expectations of 9.317 billion bushels. Soybean production had been expected slightly higher at 2.407 billion bushels.
Winter wheat seedings for the 1997 crop were estimated at 48.222 million acres, off seven percent from 1996 and the lowest planted acreage since 1978, USDA said.

Hard red winter wheat seedings were estimated at 34.1 million acres, down five percent from last year. Soft red winter wheat seedings were down sharply to just less than 10 million acres, off 15 percent from last year. White winter wheat acreage was estimated at 4.2 million acres, off five percent from 1996.
Durum wheat seedings in Arizona and California were projected at 220,000 acres, down 28 percent from 1996.
Stocks of U.S. corn on December 1 were put at 6.906 billion bushels, up 13 percent from a year ago.
Soybean stocks were estimated at 1.823 billion, down one percent from a year earlier, and all wheat stocks were pegged at 1.219 billion, down nine percent.
In domestic supply/demand estimates, USDA lowered 1996/97 corn ending stocks to 959 million bushels due to larger feed and residual use.
Soybean ending stocks were lowered to 155 million bushels because of lower production and a higher crush forecast.
Wheat ending stocks were raised to 469 million bushels because of larger imports and reduced domestic use.
